integration_decision.new_finding: Pinned runner.py writes latest.json then audit_latest.json then anata_latest.json as three separate atomic replacements after archive lock scope; the first two output schemas have no shared source_record_id generation token. An A-only pause immediately before its third anata_latest.json write permits B to publish a full rowB generation, then A to overwrite only the handoff with stale no-rowB output. This precise interleaving would expose cross-file mixed generations if executed; it is not yet proven.
integration_decision.test_contract: No network, real runner, spawn context, shared tmp_path, T=1700000000000. Child A starts with empty archive and child-local wrapper of runner.atomic_write_json: when destination name is anata_latest.json, set A_paused Event and wait bounded release_A; do not mock handoff. At A_paused, assert A alive, latest.json and audit_latest.json exist and anata_latest.json absent; snapshot A latest/audit hashes. Parent appends one valid PIT-visible BTC ETF rowB (effective=T-2000, available=observed=T-1000, source=farside_etf, source_record_id=rowB). Spawn unpatched child B; wait/join bounded, assert archive/scoring 1/1, no errors, B anata provenance rowB. Snapshot and JSON-parse B latest/audit/anata; require B latest hash differs A latest and B audit.visible_observation_count=1. Release A; wait/join bounded. Final latest/audit must equal B snapshots; final anata must equal A no-rowB handoff and differ from B snapshot, demonstrating mixed generation if observed. Require compact IPC, 10s bounded Events/Queues, exitcodes, all-three JSON parsing, whole-test finally release/terminate/join; INVALID_TEST if no pause, rowB visibility, B delta, or controlled ordering. Preserve logs. Do not modify production code.
